title: Microsoft and SAP: How we support our customers
description: Discover how Microsoft and SAP work together to provide joint support to their customers. Microsoft and SAP work closely to provide the same SLAs for support requests and have aligned teams that work together to resolve customer issues.   Learn more about running SAP applications on Azure: https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/overview/sap/  Check out the latest white papers, e-books, videos, webinars and blogs to help you on your cloud adoption journey: https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/solutions/sap/resources/

SAP and Microsoft they started their partnership roughly 25 years ago, was technology integration of back then SAP and R3 on Windows and on SQL Server and, since then, those companies share the responsibility for the success of our joint customers. . responsibility for the success of our joint customers. You need to get your stuff right there. You don't have a lot of attempts, you need to get your architectures right, you need to get the software products right, you need to get you in this case Azure infrastructure right. You get your business on the software and infrastructure you are running. You need a completely different approach to support. There is no way of saying, please wait until I have time, so you need SLA's and Microsoft and SAP share the SLA's in our integrated support process. You need fast reaction times by your support, fast response times and SLAs behind those response times and SLAs behind the support. Finger-pointing is just no solution. We have joint teams. That means I have support engineers from the Microsoft side in the SAP support line and the support process so the cases that come through the SAP channels can be handled and taken over by regular Microsoft support. We have several teams that can help SAP and SAP customers and SAP Centric System Integrators, the Azure customer advisory team is certainly for top-end customers, but then we have an Azure fast track team that helps in the medium-to- smaller area with partners and customers. ZISER SINGERMANNEN, IT SERVICES SYSTEM, INSPIRED STAFF, Q-CAM In SAP, we have the max attention customers. Those, if they move to Azure, are supported by the max attention team, which is matching, on the Microsoft side, the Azure customer advisory team. Kat is part of our joint team. The working experience was really excellent. They helped us to get the requirements that SAP has with it's customers directly implemented with Azure development and delivered to our customers. So that's also a collaboration right there because it also shows that SAP is fully committed to Azure. If you're fully committed from the Microsoft side to SAP Workload. The big benefit is the peace of mind that you get from the availability of the SAP resources together with Microsoft resources. My experience working with Microsoft is that we speak the same language if you talk about the requirements of enterprise customers.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because its apparent purpose is to explain how Microsoft and SAP coordinate enterprise customer support, including service-level agreements, response times, and joint support teams. The described benefit is coordinated technical resources and support rather than a request for payment, investment, credentials, or other financial participation. Interview-style office footage and visible Microsoft branding are consistent with this business-support context, although the sampled frames do not independently establish every affiliation or speech claim.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The primary content is an educational and operational discussion of enterprise software support, service-level agreements, and coordinated technical teams.
